results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
I built a 4-color (Jeskai plus black) Lute control deck, and the deck is legal.

**Directions I considered**
1. **Jeskai Control's shell plus black.** I took the counters, removal and card draw from Jeskai Control. A 5-0 Jeskai list (league, 2026-04-22) already runs 3 Resonating Lute with 4 Great Hall of the Biblioplex.
2. **Mardu midrange around Inevitable Defeat, splashing blue for the Lute and Revelation.** This is weaker, because the Lute's mana only works for instants and sorceries.
3. **Izzet "big X" burn.** The Lute's doubled mana goes into Traumatic Critique. This doesn't use Inevitable Defeat well.

I picked direction 1. The Lute is a mana doubler that also fixes colors, and that solves both of the other cards' problems: Inevitable Defeat costs {1}{R}{W}{B} (it needs black) and Jeskai Revelation costs 7. About 107 real lists already run Defeat and Revelation together in a Jeskai-style control deck.

**The plan**
- **Turns 1–3:** Hold the board with No More Lies, Lightning Helix, Get Lost and Day of Judgment. Dig with Consult the Star Charts and Stock Up.
- **Turn 4:** Land Resonating Lute. Every land now taps for two mana of any one color, but only for instants and sorceries.
- **Turn 5:** Five lands make 10 mana, enough for Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation in the same turn.
  - Inevitable Defeat can't be countered. It exiles their best permanent, they lose 3 life and you gain 3.
  - Jeskai Revelation returns a threat to its owner's hand, deals 4 damage, makes two 1/1 Monks, draws 2 cards and gains 4 life.
- **The kill:** Traumatic Critique with X of 10 or more, using the Lute's doubled mana.

**Mana**
- Black comes from 4 Great Hall (any color for instants), Godless Shrine, Blood Crypt, Watery Grave, Gloomlake Verge and the Lute itself.
- Counts are 18 white, 19 blue, 14 red and 8 black sources on 26 lands. That's in line with real Jeskai Control lists.
- By turn 4 you have a black source 79% of the time. You also have the Lute, Consult or Stock Up 86% of the time.

**Choices worth knowing**
- **No Ultima.** Many Jeskai lists play it, but it destroys all artifacts, including your own Lute. Day of Judgment is the sweeper instead.
- **Turn 8 is a target, not a promise.** Having drawn all five specific cards in the win line by turn 8 happens in only about 3% of games. In practice the deck wins more loosely: Helix, Defeat and Revelation drain and burn, Monk tokens attack, and any Lute turn turns into two big spells.

The 15-card sideboard covers the main decks in the field: Prowess, Landfall, Elementals and Dimir.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around The Jolly Balloon Man, Sewer-veillance Cam and Bloom Tender.
results.text:
I built a four-color Craterhoof ramp deck (brew, accepted as legal). It takes the mana-creature and Craterhoof Behemoth package from the menu's Selesnya Offense/Landfall-style green decks; the tools file it under the "Aang" strategy. The plan is to turn Balloon Man and Bloom Tender into a burst of mana and then make a second copy of whatever big creature you cast.

**How the three cards work together:**
- **Bloom Tender** taps for one mana of each color among your permanents. With Balloon Man (red and white), Cam (blue) and green creatures out, that's usually 4 mana.
- **The Jolly Balloon Man** has haste. For {1} and a tap, it makes a copy of another creature you control. The copy has haste and flying and is sacrificed at end of turn. Copying Bloom Tender gives a token that taps right away for another 4 or more mana. Late in the game it copies Craterhoof, Brightglass Gearhulk (two more tutor triggers) or Formidable Speaker (another creature tutor).
- **Sewer-veillance Cam** costs U and has flash. It untaps a creature when it enters and again when it leaves (you can sacrifice it for {3}{U} to draw two). That gives Balloon Man a second activation in the same main phase, or Bloom Tender a second tap. It's also the deck's blue permanent for Tender.

**The win:** Elves on turn 1, Tender on turn 2, Balloon Man on turn 3. On turn 4 or 5, Balloon Man copies Tender for a big pile of mana and you cast Craterhoof (or fetch it with Nature's Rhythm). Then flash in Cam to untap Balloon Man and copy Craterhoof. That's two +X/+X trample triggers at once, which is normally lethal.

**Why this direction:** I also looked at two others:
- **Simic Omniscience shell:** too slow and doesn't use Balloon Man's haste.
- **Jeskai deck built on enter-the-battlefield creatures** (Flash Thompson, Glamermite untapping Balloon Man): the cards are weak.

I searched for an infinite loop and didn't find one in Standard. Craterhoof's trigger rewards a hasty copy most, so it won.

**Honest odds and trade-offs:**
- **Odds:** You'll have Balloon Man or a tutor plus a payoff by turn 4 about 84% of the time. Drawing every exact card in the line by turn 5 is only about 1.6%, though that figure doesn't count the tutors (Nature's Rhythm, Formidable Speaker, Gearhulk). Many games will win with only part of the line.
- **Mana:** The deck plays 20 lands, against about 22.6 in the donor lists, because it runs 16 mana creatures.
- **Removal:** Main-deck interaction is light (2 Seam Rip). The sideboard has Erode, Get Lost and Meltstrider's Resolve for creature decks, Rest in Peace and Soul-Guide Lantern for graveyard decks, and Spider-Sense for the spell-heavy decks.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
I built a Boros Dwarves equipment deck. It's a brew: no published list in the last 400 days plays these three cards together. You play cheap Dwarves and turn one of them into a double striker. Dwarven Mauler cuts equip costs by 2, so Hard-Won Jitte equips to it for free (a 4-damage double striker on turn 2), and Spider-Suit adds +2/+2 for 1 more mana, making it hit for 8 a turn. Kíli draws a card when another Dwarf or Equipment enters, at most once a turn, and once you control three artifacts or legends, your first equip each turn is free. Dáin's Company looks at the top four cards for a Dwarf or Equipment (30 of the deck's cards count) and gains lifelink while you control another Dwarf.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Chosen:** Mauler carrying equipment, with Kíli and Dáin's Company as card flow, using Boros Aggro's burn and mana.
2. Going wide with Fíli the Pathfinder and The Lonely Mountain's Dwarf tokens.
3. Legends built around Mjölnir.

I picked the first because only it gets the turn-2 four-damage double striker. Its cheapest pieces cost 0–1 mana, so Kíli and Dáin's Company come down without slowing the attack.

**Deck (60)**
- **Creatures (20):** 4 Dwarven Mauler, 4 Kíli the Resourceful, 4 Dáin's Company, 3 Giott, King of the Dwarves, 3 Thorin Oakenshield, 2 Dáin Ironfoot
- **Equipment (11):** 4 Hard-Won Jitte, 4 Spider-Suit, 2 Dwarven Mattock, 1 Mjölnir, Hammer of Thor
- **Burn (7):** 4 Burst Lightning, 3 Shock. These are borrowed from Boros Aggro (Burst Lightning is in 89% of its lists, Shock in 84%) and clear blockers or finish the opponent.
- **Lands (22):** 4 Sacred Foundry, 4 Inspiring Vantage, 3 Sunbillow Verge, 2 Sundown Pass, 2 The Lonely Mountain, 4 Mountain, 3 Plains. That's 19 red sources and 16 white.

**Sideboard (15):** 3 Sear, 2 Abrade, 2 Ghost Vacuum, 2 Magebane Lizard, 2 Lightning Helix, 2 Celestial Armor, 2 Rest in Peace

**How it wins:**
- **Turn 1:** Mauler.
- **Turn 2:** Jitte, equipped for free.
- **Turn 3:** Spider-Suit on the Mauler, or Kíli.
- **After that:** Company and Kíli keep finding threats while burn removes blockers. The goal is to win on turn 5.

**Odds:** without mulligans, you'll have a Mauler by turn 3 in 49% of games, and Mauler plus Jitte or Spider-Suit in about 35%. When the Mauler is missing, Giott (who already has double strike) and Thorin carry the equipment instead.

**Choice the deck checker questioned:** it flagged Shock as rarely played (1% of decks). I kept it because it's a 1-mana instant, which leaves mana for equipping, kills Prowess's small creatures, and can hit the opponent directly.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:
I built a mono-black sacrifice deck ("aristocrats"). Your three cards are the engine and the deck drains the opponent out. It's labelled a brew because no published list runs all three together. The checker accepted it with no warnings.

**The plan:** Greedy Freebooter, Forsaken Miner and Bloodghast are creatures that come back or leave value when they die. Umbral Collar Zealot sacrifices them for free at any time. Every sacrifice turns into lost life:
- **The Sackville-Bagginses** makes the opponent lose 1 for every token you sacrifice. That includes the Treasures from Freebooter and from its own enter trigger, Rat King's Rat tokens, Infestation Sage's Insects, Scavenger's Talent's Food and Realm of Koh's Spirits.
- **Popular Egotist** drains 1 for every permanent you sacrifice, including Treasures.
- **Forsaken Miner keeps coming back.** Each of those drains targets an opponent, which counts as committing a crime, so you can pay {B} to return Miner and feed it to the Zealot again.
- **Bloodghast** comes back with each land you play.

**The best-case line:**
- Turn 1: Freebooter.
- Turn 2: Zealot.
- Turn 3: Egotist.
- Turn 4: Sackville, sacrificing Freebooter. You draw a card and get two Treasures, and every sacrifice from there drains 1–2 life.
- Turns 5–6: keep looping Miner and Bloodghast through the Zealot while you attack. Aim to finish around turn 6.

**What the odds mean:** Having every card in that exact line by turn 6 is rare (1.3%). That's fine, because any outlet or payoff plus any fodder runs the engine. You'll have at least one Zealot, Sackville or Egotist plus a fodder creature by turn 3 in about 82% of games (draw math with no mulligans).

**The three directions I considered:**
1. **Rakdos (black-red):** add Garna, Bloodfist of Keld (deals 1 damage to each opponent when your creatures die outside combat) and the menu's Mardu Discard Bloodghast package.
2. **Golgari (black-green) Food:** Scavenger's Talent plus Experimental Confectioner.
3. **Mono-black:** borrow the Mono-Black Aggro shell, which is 10 recent lists.

**Why mono-black:** Popular Egotist does Garna's job for one mana less and without a second color. All-Swamp mana also suits Bloodghast ({B}{B}), Nine-Lives Familiar ({1}{B}{B}) and the {B} payments to bring Miner back.

**What I borrowed from Mono-Black Aggro:**
- Its mana: 22 lands with 18 Swamps, plus 3 Realm of Koh as untapped Spirit-token makers. I added one Fountainport, which can sacrifice a token to draw.
- Forsaken Miner.
- Its removal, Requiting Hex and Shoot the Sheriff. Requiting Hex has an extra synergy here: its optional -1/-1 counter can go on your own Freebooter, which kills it for a Treasure.

**Sideboard:** Duress, Intimidation Tactics and Strategic Betrayal for the control and Excruciator decks. Ghost Vacuum for graveyard decks. Day of Black Sun and Bitter Triumph for the creature decks: Prowess, Landfall and Selesnya.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Gideon's Memorial, Solitary Cell and Ajani Unrelenting.
results.text:
This is a brew: **Boros Superfriends**, with 13 planeswalkers. No published list in the last 400 days plays your three cards together, so there was no shell to copy. I borrowed the mana base and removal from Boros Aggro, the most-played Boros deck (77 lists).

**How the deck works:**
- **Gideon's Memorial** costs 2 and taps for any color, but only to cast planeswalkers. That's the ramp.
- **Turn 3:** Memorial plus three lands casts Chandra, Torch of Defiance.
- **Turn 4:** Chandra's +1 adds two red mana. With four lands and Memorial, that's 7 mana, enough for **Ajani Unrelenting** (costs 6).
- **Ajani's −3** deals 4 damage to every creature except your tokens. In practice it wipes only their board, and every loyalty ability you use also makes a 2/2 token.
- **Elspeth, Storm Slayer** doubles every token you make, so each Ajani activation gives two 2/2s.
- **Memorial** gives your tokens +1/+0 and vigilance, so they can attack and still block to protect your planeswalkers.
- **Solitary Cell** exiles an early threat that costs 3 or less. It also lets you discard extra copies of legendary cards to draw. The deck has 17 legendary cards (Memorial plus all 13 walkers), so spare copies always have a use.
- **Ajani, Outland Chaperone** makes a token every turn and can kill a tapped attacker.
- **Voice of Victory** stops opponents from casting spells during your turn, so walkers don't get countered.
- **Removal:** Burst Lightning, Get Lost, Lightning Helix and Sear handle aggro decks until the walkers take over.

**Why this direction:** I compared three:
1. Boros Superfriends using Memorial as walker ramp.
2. Go-wide Boros tokens using the Boros Aggro package, with Ajani as the top end.
3. Jeskai walker control using Azorius Control's counterspells and sweepers.

I chose the first because it's the only one that uses all three cards for their actual text. Memorial's mana only goes into walkers, Cell's draw ability needs legendary cards, and Ajani's sweep spares exactly the tokens this deck makes. The other two would leave Memorial's mana or Cell's draw mostly unused.

**Honest odds:**
- You'll have Memorial by turn 5 in about 57% of games, and Ajani Unrelenting in about 46%.
- Drawing all six cards of the planned sequence (Memorial, Chandra, Ajani Unrelenting, Elspeth, Cell, Outland Chaperone) by turn 7 happens in only about 1% of games. The sequence is a best case, not a requirement. Any one or two walkers behind removal and tokens usually carries the game.

The deck runs 24 lands, and the checker passed it with no warnings. The sideboard is built for the current field:
- **Rest in Peace** against Reanimator and Sacrifice.
- **Seam Rip** against cheap threats.
- **Dawn's Truce** to protect your walkers.
- **Magebane Lizard** against control and Prowess.
- **Extra removal:** Sear, Lightning Helix and Stroke of Midnight.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Slumbering Trudge, Fight Rigging and The Great Henge.
results.text:
I built **Mono-Green Trudge Henge**, a brew. It uses the mana base and ramp from Mono-Green Devotion, but the deck runs on Slumbering Trudge's raw 6 power. No published list in any format plays your three cards together, so this is untested.

**The plan:** Cast Slumbering Trudge on turn 1 for X=0, which costs just one green. It comes in as a tapped 6/6 with 3 stun counters (each counter stops one untap). It can't attack yet, but its 6 power does two jobs:
- **The Great Henge** costs only 3 mana (two green plus one), usually on turn 3. It taps for two green the turn it lands. After that, every creature you play draws a card.
- **Fight Rigging** puts a +1/+1 counter on Trudge at the start of combat. That makes it 7 power, so you play the card Rigging set aside for free.

Kiora, Behemoth Beckoner draws a card whenever a creature with 4+ power enters, and her untap ability strips Trudge's stun counters early. Ouroboroid turns Rigging's counter into counters on your whole board, and Craterhoof Behemoth or Ghalta, Primal Hunger finish the game. Life's Legacy can sacrifice a stunned Trudge to draw 6.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Selesnya Company** (from the current meta). Collected Company can hit Trudge since its mana value is 1, but Trudge always enters with 3 stun counters that way, and the white cards don't help the 7-power plan.
2. **Simic untap**, with Kiora's Follower clearing stun counters. The second color costs too much consistency for one effect.
3. **Mono-green devotion, borrowing the menu's dork + Badgermole Cub package. I chose this one.** Eight dorks plus Badgermole Cub make the turn-3 Henge/Rigging turn real, and the shell already runs Kiora, Ouroboroid and Craterhoof, which all fit the plan.

**Honest odds:** I added 3 Nature's Rhythm as extra copies of Trudge, since Rhythm can put it straight onto the battlefield (still stunned). With them, you have a Trudge or Rhythm plus a Rigging or Henge by turn 4 in about 54% of games without a mulligan. Drawing every card in the full win line by turn 5 is near 0%, mostly because Craterhoof is a single copy. That line is the best case, not the usual game; the usual game is Henge or Rigging pulling you ahead on cards.

**Choices worth knowing:**
- **20 lands:** that's one under the devotion average of about 21; I'm counting on the 8 dorks and Henge's mana.
- **No main-deck removal:** the deck has none besides Boseiju.
- **Sideboard:** Tail Swipe and Voracious Hydra handle creatures, for Golgari, Selesnya Company and the Prowess decks. Unlicensed Hearse, Soul-Guide Lantern and Pithing Needle are for Greasefang and Phoenix. Surrak, Elusive Hunter and Cityscape Leveler are for UW Control.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Guiding Voice, Practiced Offense and Favored Hoplite.
results.text:
This is a Mono-White Heroic counters brew. You play cheap heroic creatures, then cast a stream of one-mana spells that target them. Each spell grows the creature, and Favored Hoplite also prevents all damage dealt to it that turn. Phalanx Leader turns each targeting spell into a +1/+1 counter on every creature you control. Practiced Offense finishes the game: it puts a counter on each of your creatures and gives double strike to your biggest heroic creature, which also triggers its heroic. You can flash it back for {1}{W} later.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-White heroic counters.** This is the only shell where real lists ran all three of your cards together (2 Mono-White lists).
2. **Azorius Heroic.** Add Elusive Otter, Secret Identity and Slip Out the Back.
3. **Greasefang's white package from the current results.** Seasoned Hallowblade and Sheltered by Ghosts, both already proven next to Practiced Offense.

I went with Mono-White, using parts of the third direction. Playing one colour makes Phalanx Leader's {W}{W} and the flashbacks easy to cast, and Illuminator Virtuoso turned out to be white, so I kept it. Blue would mostly add mana problems.

**How the cards fit:**
- **Favored Hoplite:** your turn-1 threat. It gets 23 targeting spells.
- **Guiding Voice:** a one-mana counter that also triggers heroic. Its learn either fetches a Lesson from the sideboard or lets you swap a dead card. The Lessons are Enter the Avatar State (protection plus lifelink), Reduce to Memory (removal), Airbender's Reversal and Academic Probation.
- **Sheltered by Ghosts:** your main way to remove a permanent. It exiles a blocker or threat and gives your attacker lifelink and ward {2}.
- **Eiganjo, Seat of the Empire:** its channel ability is a bit of extra removal.

**How it wins:** the sample line wins on turn 5:
1. Turn 1: Hoplite.
2. Turn 2: Phalanx Leader.
3. Turn 3: Guiding Voice and Homestead Courage.
4. Turn 4: Practiced Offense with double strike for a big hit.
5. Turn 5: Sheltered by Ghosts clears the way.

You'll almost never draw that exact sequence (the checker says about 1% of games), but the pieces swap freely. You see at least one heroic creature plus a targeting spell by turn 3 about 92% of the time (no mulligans counted).

**Things to know:**
- **19 lands, below the tools' suggestion.** The checker recommended about 22 and the Mono-White lists average 22.8, but those are a different, higher-curve deck. With an average mana value of 1.77 I matched Azorius Heroic's 19.5 instead. Mutavault and the two flashback spells use up spare mana.
- **Removal-heavy decks are the main risk.** Golgari Midrange (Fatal Push) and Izzet's burn are both near the top of the results. Gods Willing, Feat of Resistance, Sejiri Shelter and Hoplite's damage prevention are your answers, so hold one up when you commit a lot of counters to a single creature.
- **Sideboard:** besides the four Lessons, it has Portable Hole, Declaration in Stone, Spectacular Tactics, Elite Spellbinder and Rest in Peace for the top decks in the results.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Jeskai Revelation, Inevitable Defeat and Tablet of Discovery.
results.text:
The deck is a four-colour control brew (white, blue, red and black). Jeskai Revelation needs blue, red and white, and Inevitable Defeat needs red, white and black, so four colours is the minimum that runs both. I took the mana base and counterspells/removal from Pioneer's UW Control lists. The engine comes from real decks: when I looked up these three cards together, they only appeared in one place, 135 Standard "4C Control" lists. Those lists combine all three with Stock Up and Flashback. I moved that engine into Pioneer.

1. A three-colour Jeskai deck (white, blue, red). I ruled it out because Inevitable Defeat costs black mana.
2. Bolting the requested cards onto a Niv-Mizzet five-colour shell. I ruled it out because Niv-Mizzet Reborn only finds two-colour cards, and both requested spells are three-colour.
3. **The one I chose:** the Standard 4C engine in Pioneer, using UW Control's interaction (No More Lies, Consult the Star Charts, Supreme Verdict, Get Lost, The Wandering Emperor) and Pioneer's shock lands, triomes and Verges for mana. It keeps your three cards at the centre and uses the best-tested pieces from both decks.

**The plan:**
- **Turns 1–4:** survive with No More Lies, Lightning Helix, Sear and Supreme Verdict, and dig with Stock Up and Consult the Star Charts.
- **Tablet of Discovery:** its {R}{R} can only pay for instants and sorceries, and 29 of this deck's spells are exactly that. Cast on turn 3, it lets you cast Revelation (7 mana) on turn 5.
- **Inevitable Defeat:** removal that can't be countered and can be cast at instant speed. It exiles their best permanent and drains them for 3.
- **Jeskai Revelation:** bounces something, deals 4 damage, makes two 1/1 Monks with prowess, draws two cards and gains 4 life. Flashback ({R}) lets you cast it a second time from the graveyard. Two Revelations plus the Monks and The Wandering Emperor are how you win, usually around turn 8.

**Mana:** 26 lands, with 17 white, 17 blue, 17 red and 9 black sources. Great Hall of the Biblioplex counts as any colour, but only for instants and sorceries. The deck check found no errors or warnings.

**Things to know:**

- **Removal:** Lightning Bolt and Journey to Nowhere handle opposing creatures.

**Plan:** Play Mascot on turn 2. Then loop the Eidolons through your graveyard with cheap gold spells. Each loop gets past a blocker or prevents damage, and makes Mascot bigger. Bolt and Lava Dart finish the game around turn 5–6.

**The three directions I considered:**
1. Boros hybrid/gold aggro, using the Boros Aggro shell's lands and its Thrilling Discovery and Lunarch Veteran.
2. A slower Jeskai Control version with the Eidolons as blockers that keep coming back.
3. A Mono-Red Rally shell with a white splash.

I picked option 1 because only Boros has enough cheap multicolored commons to keep both Eidolons coming back, and Spirit Mascot is red-white anyway.

**Things to know:**
- **Mana:** 18 lands with 12 white and 11 red sources. That's less white than real Boros Aggro lists (about 16), because this deck needs both colors about equally.
- **Mascot draw odds:** you see Mascot by turn 4 in about 53% of games. You find something that grows it about 96% of the time.
- **The sample win line** (every named card drawn by turn 6) only comes together about 1.5% of the time. That's not the plan you should expect. The deck has many copies of each piece, so other combinations work the same way.
- **Weakness:** the 4-mana Eidolons are weak cards on their own. Most of their value comes from coming back to your hand over and over.

The sideboard targets the biggest decks right now: Pyroblast for Terror and Faeries, Electrickery for Elves and the small-creature decks, Dust to Dust for Affinity and Wildfire, and Prismatic Strands for Madness and Rally.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Future Sight, Academy Rector and Veteran Explorer.
results.text:
The deck is in: a five-color Survival-and-Rector combo deck built around Future Sight. It's labeled a brew because no published list in the last 400 days plays all three of your cards together.

**The plan:** Veteran Explorer comes down on turn 1. On turn 2, cast Cabal Therapy and flash it back by sacrificing Explorer. That fetches two untapped basics, so you have 4 lands on turn 2 and can still cast Goblin Bombardment with the extra mana. With 5 lands on turn 3, you can hard-cast Future Sight (Explorer can grab Islands for its UUU). Or play Academy Rector, sacrifice it whenever you like, and put Future Sight, Survival of the Fittest or Pattern of Rebirth straight onto the battlefield. From there it's a value engine. Every Survival or Rector search shuffles your library, so Future Sight shows you a fresh card each time. Survival finds Karmic Guide, Deranged Hermit and Symbiotic Wurm. You win by sacrificing everything to Bombardment, then flashing in Caller of the Claw for a 2/2 Bear per nontoken creature that died that turn, and throwing those at the opponent too.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Tradewind Survival** (blue-green Survival with Opposition), with white added for Rector. Without black or red it has almost no way to sacrifice your own creatures, so Rector and Explorer would rarely die when you want them to.
2. **Living Death**, the deck that plays Veteran Explorer most (10 lists). Future Sight and Rector don't really fit its plan.
3. **The Pattern Combo shell** (I chose this). It's the only published deck that runs Rector and Explorer together. It brings sacrifice outlets (Cabal Therapy, Bombardment, Phyrexian Tower), Survival to tutor up whichever piece you're missing, and a real Bombardment kill. Future Sight slots in naturally as Rector's main target.

**Honest numbers:**
- By turn 3 on the play, you see Explorer or Survival 75% of the time and a sacrifice outlet 75% of the time. You have both 55% of the time.
- By turn 4, you see Future Sight, Rector or Survival 89% of the time.
- The checker says every card in the exact line is drawn by turn 6 in only 0.1% of games. That's because it doesn't simulate tutors: Survival, Rector and Pattern stand in for most of the pieces. Still, expect this to grind out a win around turn 6 rather than kill fast.

**Notes:**
- The checker flagged Goblin Bombardment as rarely played. I kept it because here it's your free, repeatable way to sacrifice creatures and your win condition, not removal.
- Explorer gives the opponent lands too, and in a field that's 16% Stiflenought, expect it to get Stifled.
- The mana works for five colors (12 white, 12 blue, 8 black, 8 red and 15 green sources). The 10 basics are there so Explorer can fix colors as well as ramp.
- The sideboard includes enchantments Rector can fetch: Engineered Plague for Goblins and Worship for Sligh and Zoo.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Utopia Tree, Rhystic Tutor and Bloodfire Colossus.
results.text:
I've built and submitted the brew: **BRG Colossus Reanimator**. No published list in the last 400 days plays these three cards together, so this is a new deck, not a copy of an existing one.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Hermit Druid shell** (from your list of top decks). Utopia Tree stands in for Birds of Paradise. Colossus is just one more creature to bring back from the graveyard, and the deck's actual win needs a pile of one-ofs that have nothing to do with your cards.
2. **Jund ramp that pays full price for Colossus.** Utopia Tree, rituals and Rhystic Tutor push toward an 8-mana spell. It's too slow against Stiflenought and Goblins.
3. **Reanimator shell, splashing green and red.** This is the one I picked, because it's the only plan where Colossus's 8-mana cost doesn't matter. It's built on the Reanimator package from 52 real lists (Putrid Imp, Dark Ritual, Cabal Therapy, Exhume, Reanimate, Animate Dead, Buried Alive, Lotus Petal).

**The plan:** Get Colossus into the graveyard by discarding it to Putrid Imp, or with Buried Alive or Survival of the Fittest. Then bring it back with Exhume, Reanimate or Animate Dead, ideally on turn 2. It attacks as a 6/6. When the opponent is at 6 life or less, or their board gets in the way, pay R and sacrifice it to deal 6 damage to each creature and each player. That sends it back to the graveyard, so the next reanimation spell brings it back for another blast.

**What each requested card does here:**
- **Rhystic Tutor** finds whichever half of the combo you're missing.
- **Utopia Tree** makes the colours the deck can't easily get: green for Survival, and the R to sacrifice Colossus. It also lets you cast the 3-mana spells on turn 2, and you can sacrifice it to flash back Cabal Therapy.

**Things to know:**
- **Odds:** You'll see a way to bin Colossus plus a way to bring it back by turn 3 about 76% of the time (14 cards put it in the graveyard, 10 bring it back).
- **Life total:** Reanimate costs you 8 life on Colossus, and each blast hits you for 6 too. Use Exhume or Animate Dead when you're low.
- **Exhume:** It lets the opponent return a creature too, but a Colossus blast usually kills it.
- **Symbiotic Wurm (1 copy):** It's a backup creature to bring back. As a 7/7 it survives your own blast.
- **Land count:** The checker suggested about 21 lands. I kept 16 lands plus 3 Lotus Petal and 4 Utopia Tree, which is already more than the 14 that real Reanimator lists average.

**Sideboard:**
- Duress and Unmask against Stiflenought's counterspells.
- Snuff Out and Pyroclasm against Goblins and Sligh.
- Naturalize against Enchantress and Replenish.
- Phantom Nishoba as a lifelinking creature to bring back against burn.
